identity.title: Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training

problem.claim: LLM pre-training needs open data that can be used legally and complies with data-security regulations.

gap.claim: Existing large-scale datasets are described as containing substantial copyrighted or proprietary content, leaving a need for truly open alternatives.

contributions.claim: Introduces Common Corpus, an author-described large open pre-training dataset containing about two trillion tokens from uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data.
Provides broad language coverage, including rarely represented low-resource languages, and includes substantial code data.
Reports detailed data provenance, filtering, and curation procedures.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Common Corpus as the largest open dataset for LLM pre-training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that two small language models trained on Common Corpus perform comparably to other models of their size, indicating suitability for multilingual pre-training.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large pre-training corpora raise legal-use concerns because they may include copyrighted or proprietary material.
Common Corpus is presented as an open, approximately two-trillion-token alternative assembled from uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data.
The dataset spans high- and low-resource languages, includes code, and is accompanied by provenance, filtering, and curation details.
Two small trained models are reported to match similarly sized models, supporting the dataset’s stated multilingual pre-training suitability.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a dataset’s legal-status description with provenance, filtering, curation, and a small-model comparison.

lessons.interpretation: This links resource construction claims to both auditability and an initial use demonstration.
lessons.application: For a data-resource paper, explicitly connect licensing and provenance documentation to a concrete downstream training comparison.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the contribution is purely theoretical or when downstream training is outside scope.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the two models’ sizes, evaluation tasks, metrics, baselines, or uncertainty, limiting interpretation of the comparison.
It does not provide the detailed licensing, regulatory, filtering, or provenance evidence needed to assess the dataset’s legal and security claims.
The basis and comparison set for the “largest” distinction are not given.
